non_expert_title: How to research the interplay of physics and biology better
title: Advancing mechanobiology from single molecules to complex cellular systems
public_text: We still understand far too little about how physical forces shape living tissues. With my co-authors, I argue for better experimental models, measurement tools, and theories to connect mechanics from molecules to tissues.
expert_text: We argue for an integrated, multiscale mechanobiology that combines physiologically relevant multicellular reference systems, quantitative mechanical perturbation and readout, and theory/AI to connect molecular mechanics with tissue- and organism-level function.

non_expert_title: DNA particles as tiny mechanical probes in tissues
title: Mechanically programmable DNA hydrogel microparticles for 3D cellular systems
public_text: The main author used DNA as a building block for micrometre-sized particles with controlled mechanical properties. I contributed to their mechanical characterization; such particles can serve as embedded probes for how 3D tissues feel and deform.
expert_text: Fully DNA-based, sequence-programmable hydrogel microparticles with tunable size, stiffness, viscoelasticity, and cell-adhesive ligands can be integrated into fibroblast spheroids to probe and perturb mechanics in 3D culture.

non_expert_title: How tiny carbon pores sort molecules
title: Molecular determinants of solvent nanoseparation by nanoporous carbon materials
public_text: Computer simulations show that carbon materials separate solvents best when their pores are just large enough for selected molecules to pass. I contributed modelling that tracks molecular pathways through the material, helping explain how pore size and surface chemistry control separation.
expert_text: Coarse-grained simulations show optimal solvent nanoseparation near the size-exclusion threshold, with surface oxidation strongly modulating polar-molecule transport. My Markov-state modelling contribution maps transport pathways and links separation performance to pore architecture and surface chemistry.

non_expert_title: How cells sense soft and slow materials
title: Piezo1 regulates the mechanotransduction of soft matrix viscoelasticity
public_text: This study asks how cells sense materials that are not just soft, but also relax over time. It identifies Piezo1 as part of the machinery that helps cells respond to viscoelastic environments.
expert_text: The work connects Piezo1-mediated mechanotransduction to cellular responses on soft viscoelastic matrices, indicating that ion-channel-based mechanosensing contributes to how cells decode time-dependent matrix mechanics.

title: High-speed quantitative nanomechanical mapping by photothermal off-resonance AFM
public_text: We present an AFM method that maps mechanical properties much faster by moving the probe with light instead of relying only on slower piezo motion. This makes quantitative nanomechanical mapping more practical for many materials.
expert_text: Photothermal off-resonance tapping accelerates force-spectroscopy-based nanomechanical mapping by at least an order of magnitude. By modelling the probe’s thermal and mechanical response, the method recovers quantitative probe motion for rapid mapping of polymeric and metallic samples.

Hydrodynamic function and spring constant calibration of FluidFM micropipette cantilevers
public_text: FluidFM cantilevers are tiny hollow force sensors, but their special geometry makes calibration difficult. This work provides a more reliable way to determine their stiffness, which is essential for quantitative force and cell measurements.
expert_text: The study experimentally determines the hydrodynamic function of hollow FluidFM micropipette cantilevers and adapts a spring-constant calibration that uses air/liquid resonance frequencies. This avoids noisy Q-factor estimates in the Sader method and improves force calibration.

non_expert_title: Weighing cells and listening to their mechanics
title: Monitoring the mass, eigenfrequency, and quality factor of mammalian cells
public_text: We show that a vibrating microcantilever can measure not only cell mass, but also how a cell mechanically resonates and dissipates energy. This links cell growth and cell mechanics in one measurement.
expert_text: Ångström-scale microcantilever oscillations are used to monitor living cells across applied frequency ranges, extracting total mass, eigenfrequency, and quality factor. The work shows when apparent mass depends on cellular mechanical response and damping.

non_expert_title: What makes water pass through tiny channels
title: Entropic barrier of water permeation through single-file channels
public_text: This paper looks at the energetic cost for water molecules to pass single-file through narrow biological channels. It helps explain how aquaporins move water so quickly while still facing molecular-scale barriers.
expert_text: Activation-energy measurements and single-channel permeability estimates for Aquaporin-1 are used to estimate the entropic contribution to water permeation. The result links a small entropic barrier to an efficient water-conduction rate of around 10^10 molecules per second.

title: Tailoring microcantilever sensitivity to monitor single adherent living cells
public_text: This work improves how microcantilevers can monitor single adherent living cells by tuning their sensitivity. Better cantilevers make it easier to follow small changes in cell mass or mechanics over time.
expert_text: The study tailors microcantilever sensitivity for monitoring single adherent cells, improving the mechanical readout needed for picobalance-style measurements. It connects cantilever design and calibration to quantitative single-cell monitoring.

title: Vaccinia virus hijacks EGFR signalling to enhance virus spread
public_text: This study shows that vaccinia virus helps itself spread by making infected cells move more directionally. It hijacks growth-factor signalling so infection can advance through tissue more efficiently.
expert_text: VACV VGF is secreted from early infected cells, cleaved by ADAM10, and acts mainly in trans to activate EGFR/MAPK/FAK-dependent motility at the infection front. VGF or F11 deletion and pathway inhibitors reduce radial velocity, directional migration, and viral spread in vitro and in vivo.

non_expert_title: Putting viruses onto chosen single cells
title: Virus stamping for targeted single-cell infection
public_text: Virus stamping is a way to infect exactly selected single cells instead of a whole population. Viruses are carried on a tiny pipette or magnetic particles and placed directly onto target cells in culture, tissue, or even living animals.
expert_text: The method reversibly binds viruses to functionalized glass pipette tips or magnetic nanoparticles and delivers them by mechanical or magnetic contact to chosen cells. It enables targeted single-cell infection with different or multiple viral vectors across cell culture, mouse retina, human brain organoids, and live mouse brain.

non_expert_title: Weighing living cells in real time
title: Inertial picobalance reveals fast mass fluctuations in mammalian cells
public_text: We built a tiny balance that can follow the mass of living adherent cells over days with millisecond timing. It revealed that cell mass fluctuates rapidly by a few percent, linked to energy production and water transport.
expert_text: An optically excited microresonator picobalance measures adherent-cell mass under culture conditions with picogram sensitivity and millisecond time resolution. It detects intrinsic 1-4% mass fluctuations, links them to ATP synthesis and water transport, and shows vaccinia infection arrests growth while fluctuations persist.

non_expert_title: Building a bridge between cold atoms and tiny mechanics
title: Millikelvin all-fiber cavity optomechanical apparatus
public_text: This early physics work built an instrument to couple ultracold atoms to a tiny mechanical oscillator inside a cryogenic setup. It belongs to my path from precision physics toward measuring living systems.
expert_text: The apparatus combines an in-situ adjustable all-fiber membrane-in-the-middle cavity inside an ultra-high-vacuum dilution refrigerator with ultracold rubidium atoms. It produces Bose-Einstein condensates of about 2 x 10^6 atoms in under 20 s and achieves strong single-photon optomechanical coupling with a high mechanical quality factor.
